clue.text: Bent young dandy went ahead

parts.note: a buck is an old word for a fashionable young man
led means went in front, took the lead

explanation.surface: A fashionable young man strode on ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something buckled has been bent out of shape under pressure, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wave possibly in stream

definitions.meaning: a beckoning gesture, of which a wave is one example
in northern England a ... is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: Someone waves from the water of a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Beck is both a summoning gesture (as in 'at one's beck and call') and a northern English word for a brook.

clue.text: Have negotiations with one hiding in tree

indicators.note: one piece is concealed inside the word for negotiating, so it goes within it

parts.note: to confer is to hold talks or discuss
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Talks are held with someone hidden up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as a pine or fir, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Faithful, say, when taken in by deception

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being contained inside it, so the example goes into the word for deception

parts.note: a lie is a deception
say introduces an example, abbreviated EG (for example)

explanation.surface: A loyal follower is fooled by a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Liege as an adjective means loyal, owing feudal allegiance, as with a liege man to his lord.

clue.text: Out of control, soap slid off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bar of soap shoots out of someone's grip and slides away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' is a link: the answer is made out of SOAP SLID jumbled by 'off'. 'Out of control' reads as one phrase, but only 'control' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something at your disposal means having it under your control or command, so the two nouns share that sense.

clue.text: A companion on trip providing something to eat

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the article and companion follow the trip

parts.note: a spin is a short trip or ride, as in a spin in the car
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend comes along on an outing that supplies a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means coming after, so the trip is written first. The Companion of Honour is a British order awarded for national service.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, so it is one example of food.

clue.text: Drain off stock

definitions.meaning: to pour liquid off through a sieve
a breed or line of descent of animals or plants

explanation.surface: A cook pours away the liquid from a pan of stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain means both to filter off liquid and a line of descent, a breed or stock of animals.

clue.text: Rudeness without a word being spoken: one should give way to love

indicators.note: giving way means stepping aside for another, so the letter for one is replaced by the letter for love

parts.note: to act in silence is to act with nothing said
the Roman numeral for one is I
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A silent snub in which one person yields to another out of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude and disrespectful behaviour, so it is a close synonym of rudeness.

clue.text: Lover brings in new decorator

indicators.note: the lover brings something inside, so the abbreviation goes into that word

parts.note: an adorer is one who loves or worships

explanation.surface: A romantic partner invites a fresh interior designer into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An adorner is one who adorns or embellishes, which is what a decorator does.

clue.text: Perhaps stalking animal will eat another, chaps!

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the deer word swallows the next two pieces

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
another animal, here the ass or donkey
men is a plain synonym of chaps

explanation.surface: An alarmed cry that a predator is about to devour a second creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will eat' means the first animal swallows the others, so the deer is split open around the rest; 'Perhaps' marks stalking as only one kind of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalking, persistently following and pestering someone, is one form of harassment, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: King Edward's against having gold band on shield

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a fess is a broad horizontal band across a heraldic shield
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A monarch opposes a gold stripe being put on his coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. FESS and OR are heraldic terms, which the shield helps signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was the English king canonised in 1161, so the epithet names him.

clue.text: Track not good beyond double bend

indicators.note: beyond means further along, so the word for not good comes after the letter

parts.note: the letter S is shaped like a double bend, as on a road sign
poor means not good

explanation.surface: A trail that is hard to follow past a winding stretch of road.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or trail left by an animal, used by hunters following it.

clue.text: If Arsenal does badly, that team may not be seen as Europe's best!

definitions.text: that team may not be seen as Europe's best

indicators.note: something done badly goes wrong, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: If a top English club plays poorly, a minnow might not look like the continent's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is part of the anagram fodder, not a verb of the surface. The Faeroe Islands' football side is one of Europe's weakest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faeroe Islands field a national football team famous for losing, hardly the best side in Europe.

clue.text: As umpire, act over fielder's attitude

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed on top, so the first piece sits above the fielder

parts.note: a cricket umpire is said to stand in a match
point is a fielding position in cricket, square on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire takes against a fielder's manner.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, umpires 'stand' in a match, and point is a fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is a point of view or position on a matter, the same as an attitude.

clue.text: Final stint — pub almost closing with beer running short

parts.note: a term is a fixed period of work or office, a stint

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the pub word goes

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: running short means lacking its end, so the beer word loses its last letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A last shift at the bar before closing time, with the ale nearly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts INN to IN; 'running short' cuts ALE to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal as an adjective means last or at the end, as in a terminal stage.

clue.text: Declaration of passion for fellow may be heard in isolated part of kingdom

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are spoken aloud and sound like the answer

parts.note: someone declaring love for a man might say 'I love a man'

explanation.surface: A heartfelt confession of love that carries to a remote corner of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, a detached part of the British Isles.

clue.text: Chamber with drink approached by worker

indicators.note: the drink is approached by the worker, who comes up in front of it

parts.note: a worker ant is the stock crossword worker
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A room with liquor in it that a labourer heads towards.
explanation.definitionFit: An antrum is an anatomical cavity or chamber, especially a sinus in a bone.

clue.text: Lawyer's instrument

definitions.meaning: in England a ... is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge
a woodwind instrument blown at one end

explanation.surface: A tool belonging to a solicitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorder names both a part-time judge drawn from the legal profession and a simple woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Celebration's ending with a prize jelly

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the palm is a symbol of victory, a prize, as in to bear the palm

explanation.surface: A party finishes with someone winning a wobbly dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is petrol thickened into a sticky jelly for use in incendiary weapons.

clue.text: Clause in contract is very poor, in need of redrafting

indicators.note: redrafting means writing out again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poorly written condition in an agreement needs to be rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or qualifying clause attached to an agreement.

clue.text: It's safe to criticise a fellow that remains immature

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it harmless to have a go at a man who never grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is old underworld slang, as in a 'peterman', a safe-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is J M Barrie's boy who never grew up, used for any adult who stays childish.

clue.text: Bits of plastic maybe left in carpet badly laid

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the jumbled floor covering
a carpet laid badly is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fragments of plastic perhaps abandoned in a poorly fitted rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly laid' rearranges CARPET to PECTRA, and 'in' puts L inside after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectra (plural of plectrum) are picks for plucking strings, often made of plastic, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Firm providing flat across front of building

indicators.note: one word stretching across another surrounds it, so the stale word goes round the letter

parts.note: stale means flat, as beer goes flat or stale

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A company supplies an apartment across the front of an office block.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable as an adjective means firm and steady, not likely to give way.

clue.text: For drink I want no tea brewed inaccurately — each component should be this!

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: tea brewed badly comes out wrong, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants a drink but not badly made tea, whose ingredients ought to be balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' is a link: I wants NO TEA, and the three letters plus NO TEA are rearranged into IONATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportionate means in correct relation in size or amount, which each ingredient in a mixture should be.

clue.text: Not liking the elderly? Have a heart!

annotationWithheld.why: Not liking the elderly? Have a heart! (5): AGEIST less an E gives AGIST, but no clue word defines AGIST (to graze livestock for hire) and 'Have a heart' would have to be both a definition and the deletion signal
annotationWithheld.clue: Not liking the elderly? Have a heart!

clue.text: King and Fool become closer

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
nit is a colloquial word for a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A monarch and his jester grow more intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to draw together or unite closely, as broken bones knit or a community knits.

clue.text: I would go to 14, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
14 down is a Crown dependency, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: Someone says they would travel to an island, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 refers to the answer at 14 down, whose standard abbreviation is IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression or a characteristic way of speaking.

clue.text: Duke's estate in which a shuttle service operates?

definitions.text: Duke's estate in which a shuttle service operates?

parts.words: Duke's estate in which a shuttle service operates?
parts.note: the Duke of Beaufort's country house in Gloucestershire gave its name to the game where a shuttlecock is served over a net, not a transport shuttle

explanation.surface: A nobleman's grounds are served by a regular shuttle bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'shuttle service' is not transport but the serve of a shuttlecock; the game took its name from the Duke of Beaufort's country seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton House is the Beaufort family seat, and the racket game invented there bears its name.

clue.text: Short attempt has little weight behind it, resulting in defeat

indicators.note: the weight comes behind the attempt, so it follows it
short means cut off at the end, so the attempt word loses its last letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A brief effort with little behind it ends in losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat heavily and decisively, a stronger synonym of defeat as a verb.

clue.text: Take back soldiers to territory

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
a tract is an expanse of land, a territory

explanation.surface: An army recaptures its troops' former land.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to withdraw a statement or to draw back, so it means take back.
